tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a centrifuge for a dewatering run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: solid bowl centrifuge with polymer feed and a cake auger discharge.

cards.label: Inspect the bowl area, guards, and discharge chute and confirm all guards are fitted
Start polymer flow and confirm it reaches the feed pipe
Raise feed to the planned rate once cake discharge is steady and dry
Start sludge feed at a low rate and watch torque and vibration readings
Check lubricating oil level and cooling water supply
Start the centrifuge empty and bring it up to operating speed

tasks.explanation: Guards and lubrication come before rotation, the machine reaches speed empty, and feed rises only after a steady discharge is proven.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing over a full dewatered cake container.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake container under the press discharge is full during a run.

cards.label: Move the full container to the storage pad and record its weight or volume
Stop the sludge and polymer feeds and let the press clear
Restart the conveyor, polymer, and sludge feeds in start up order
Log the changeover time and the container identification in the solids record
Stop the cake conveyor once the last cake has discharged
Place an empty container under the discharge and confirm alignment

tasks.explanation: The press clears before it stops, the full container is recorded before it leaves, and restart follows the normal start up order.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a dewatering run using a screw press on digested sludge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screw press dewatering digested sludge for hauling to the approved outlet.

cards.label: Start the screw press and then the sludge feed at a low rate
Adjust feed and polymer by watching cake dryness and filtrate clarity
Confirm the digested sludge feed tank level and mix the tank contents
Start polymer feed and set the dose from the last successful run
Sample the cake for the run record and log feed volume and run time
Start the discharge conveyor and place the receiving container

tasks.explanation: Feed is mixed and containment is ready before the press starts, dose starts from proven settings, and adjustments follow cake appearance.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for troubleshooting a belt press that is producing very wet cake.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake solids have fallen sharply, press settings unchanged since the last good run.

cards.label: Reduce the sludge feed rate to give the press more drainage time
Sample the feed sludge and check whether its solids concentration has fallen
Check polymer supply, age, and delivery rate against the run sheet
Escalate to the supervisor with samples and records if cake is still wet
Inspect the belts for blinding and wash them if the spray pattern is poor
Resample the cake after the changes have had time to take effect

tasks.explanation: Feed, polymer, and belt condition are checked in that order before rate is cut, and escalation carries evidence rather than opinion.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing sludge drying beds for a new filling cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outdoor sand drying beds at a small western plant, summer season.

cards.label: Remove the dried sludge from the previous cycle to the storage area
Record the bed number, date, volume applied, and feed solids in the solids log
Open the filling valve in stages and spread sludge evenly across the bed
Level the sand surface and repair any cracked sidewalls
Check the underdrain outlet and confirm it is clear and draining to the plant inlet
Inspect the sand surface and replace or top up sand where it is thin or fouled

tasks.explanation: Old sludge and bed repairs come before filling, the underdrain is proven clear first, and the record ties the bed to its load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for deciding when a drying bed load is ready to remove.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sludge has been on the bed for several weeks in dry weather.

cards.label: Schedule removal and hauling while the bed is at its driest
Test the sample for solids content against the hauling requirement
Take a core sample through the full sludge depth
Check the weather forecast for rain that would rewet the sludge
Inspect the surface for cracking and separation from the bed walls
Record the removal date, mass hauled, and the outlet used in the solids log

tasks.explanation: Appearance is confirmed by a solids test, weather is checked before scheduling, and the haul record closes the bed cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a weekly dewatering equipment care round.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: press room round covering the press, polymer system, pumps, and conveyors.

cards.label: Run the press wash water and inspect spray nozzles for blockages
Check sludge feed pump operation, seals, and discharge pressure
Check polymer tank level, mixers, and day tank condition
Record findings and raise work orders for any defect in the maintenance log
Test the press room sump pump and high level alarm
Check conveyor belts, bearings, and cake discharge path for build up

tasks.explanation: The round moves from chemical supply to discharge so a fault is found at its source, alarms are tested, and defects become work orders.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a chlorine contact tank disinfection program at the beginning of the discharge season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal discharge plant in western Canada preparing for its spring effluent release.

cards.label: Adjust the dose to hold the target residual and record the seasonal start up
Sample effluent for residual and bacteriological testing through the first days of discharge
Confirm chlorine supply, feed pump operation, and spare parts are on hand
Start chlorine feed at the low end of the approved dose range
Fill and flush the contact tank and check for leaks or short circuit paths
Inspect the contact tank, baffles, and chlorine feed equipment after the off season

tasks.explanation: Equipment and supply are proven before the tank is filled, feed starts low, and bacteriological results confirm the program before discharge settles in.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine chlorine residual control check on final effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: continuous effluent disinfection with a chlorine feed paced to flow.

cards.label: Adjust the feed pump in one small step if the residual is outside the range
Resample after one contact time has passed to confirm the new residual
Collect an effluent sample at the residual sampling point after the contact tank
Measure total chlorine residual with the bench kit and record the result
Log the dose, flow, and both residuals in the disinfection record
Compare the residual with the target range and the recent effluent flow

tasks.explanation: The residual is measured before any adjustment, one step is given a full contact time to take effect, and the confirming sample closes the check.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing an empty chlorine gas cylinder safely with a second operator present.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one tonne style container is not used here, this is a small cylinder system with a vacuum regulator.

cards.label: Close the cylinder valve and the feed line valve on the empty cylinder
Remove the vacuum regulator following the site procedure and cap the cylinder outlet
Put on the required protective equipment and confirm the emergency kit and ventilation are available
Move the empty cylinder to the storage area and secure the full cylinder in its place
Fit the regulator with a new gasket and test the connection for leaks with the approved method
Open the cylinder, restore feed, and confirm chlorine flow and residual response

tasks.explanation: Protection and ventilation come before valves are touched, leak testing precedes feed restoration, and residual response proves the change worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for verifying ultraviolet disinfection performance during a weekly check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: open channel ultraviolet system disinfecting final effluent.

cards.label: Record flow, lamp hours, and intensity readings from the control panel
Log the check, any lamp change, and the effluent results together
Wipe or confirm automatic cleaning of the quartz sleeves if the design requires it
Check effluent samples results for the week against the disinfection target
Clean or replace any lamp flagged by the panel alarms
Compare the panel intensity with a reference sensor check if one is provided

tasks.explanation: Panel data is recorded before cleaning so fouling can be judged, effluent results are reviewed with the readings, and lamp work is logged with its evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding when effluent bacteriological results exceed the target after disinfection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: laboratory reports a high bacteriological result on a routine effluent sample, discharge continues under provincial requirements.

cards.label: Check chlorine residual records or ultraviolet intensity records for the sample period
Inspect the contact tank or ultraviolet channel for fouling, high flow, or bypass
Notify the supervisor promptly under the plant notification procedure
Resample the effluent at the same point using full sterile technique
Increase disinfection intensity as directed and track follow up results until they return to range
Confirm the result details, sample date, and sampling point with the laboratory

tasks.explanation: The result is verified and the supervisor notified before field work, records are checked before equipment is blamed, and follow up sampling proves the correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for calibrating a chlorine feed pump by drawdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: diaphragm feed pump drawing from a graduated calibration column.

cards.label: Calculate the delivered volume per hour from the drawdown and the time
Repeat the drawdown once to confirm the adjusted delivery and log both tests
Compare the delivery with the setpoint chart and adjust the stroke if needed
Run the pump for the timed test period and record the ending level
Line up the calibration column and fill it to the top mark from the supply tank
Record the starting level and start the pump at its normal stroke setting

tasks.explanation: Delivery is measured before it is judged, adjustment follows the calculation, and a repeat test confirms the new setting.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a sodium hypochlorite day tank refill.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bulk hypochlorite delivery filling the storage tank that feeds the day tank.

cards.label: Put on chemical protective equipment and confirm the eyewash station is working
Confirm the delivery paperwork matches the product and strength ordered
Connect the delivery hose and open valves in the order on the site procedure
Monitor the tank level during filling and stop at the planned level
Close valves, drain and disconnect the hose safely, and record the volume received
Check available tank capacity so the delivery cannot overfill the tank

tasks.explanation: Paperwork and protection come before any connection, capacity is proven before filling starts, and level monitoring prevents overfill.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a chlorine contact tank out of service for cleaning while disinfection continues.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twin contact tanks, one stays in service to maintain disinfection.

cards.label: Shift all effluent flow to the tank staying in service and verify residual
Remove accumulated solids and wash the tank and baffles
Isolate and drain the tank being removed and apply lockout to its equipment
Refill the cleaned tank, return it to standby, and restore the normal flow split
Inspect baffles and walls and report any damage before refilling
Confirm the remaining tank can hold the required contact time at current flow

tasks.explanation: Contact time in the remaining tank is proven before flow shifts, cleaning and inspection happen while the tank is empty, and normal splitting returns last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a monthly disinfection system review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor and operator review dose, residuals, bacteriological results, and chemical use for the month.

cards.label: Compile all bacteriological results and flag any result outside the target
Agree on dose range or maintenance changes for the next month
Identify days where residual or results drifted and match them to flow or quality events
Total chemical used and compare it with the volume treated
File the review with the monthly compliance summary
Compile daily dose, flow, and residual records for the month

tasks.explanation: Dose, results, and chemical use are compiled before patterns are judged, drift days are matched to events, and agreed changes close the review.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for restoring disinfection after a chlorine feed failure is repaired.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: feed pump failed for several hours, repair is complete, effluent continued to flow.

cards.label: Collect a bacteriological sample to verify disinfection has recovered
Notify the supervisor of the outage length and the recovery results for the compliance record
Increase residual checks for the next day to confirm stability
Sample effluent residual after one contact time and confirm it is in range
Restart chlorine feed at the approved dose for current flow
Confirm the repair and test the pump delivery by drawdown before returning it to service

tasks.explanation: The pump is proven before it is trusted, residual recovery precedes bacteriological confirmation, and the outage is documented for the compliance record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up an aeration basin for nitrification after a cold period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent ammonia has risen during cold weather, plant has aeration control and wasting control.

cards.label: Confirm ammonia rise with laboratory results and wastewater temperature records
Confirm dissolved oxygen is held in the upper part of the target range in all zones
Check alkalinity in the effluent to confirm buffering remains for nitrification
Raise the solids retention time target by reducing wasting in steps
Record the winter nitrification settings for reuse next season
Track ammonia daily and hold further wasting cuts once ammonia turns down

tasks.explanation: Ammonia and temperature evidence comes first, inventory and oxygen are raised together, alkalinity is checked as the safeguard, and daily tracking shows the turn.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for creating an anoxic zone routine for denitrification in an existing basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first basin zone can be unaerated with mixing, supervisor has approved a trial.

cards.label: Watch dissolved oxygen in the zone fall to near zero while later zones stay aerobic
Adjust zone air or recycle based on results and record the trial settings
Review effluent nitrate results to confirm denitrification is needed
Turn off air to the first zone and confirm mixers keep solids in suspension
Sample nitrate at the zone outlet and ammonia at the basin outlet through the trial
Confirm internal recycle or return flow brings nitrate into the anoxic zone

tasks.explanation: Need is proven by nitrate results, the zone is made anoxic without settling, and paired nitrate and ammonia sampling judges whether the trial helps or harms.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking alkalinity consumption when nitrification is active.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator awareness check using influent and effluent alkalinity and ammonia results supplied by the laboratory.

cards.label: Estimate alkalinity consumed using the factor given on the process sheet
Compare consumed alkalinity with the alkalinity entering in the influent
Confirm the effluent still carries residual alkalinity above the plant minimum
Report any shortfall to the supervisor for a chemical feed decision
Trend the check weekly while nitrification is required
Collect the laboratory ammonia removed and alkalinity results for the same period

tasks.explanation: Consumption is estimated from measured ammonia removal, the comparison with influent alkalinity shows the margin, and a shortfall is escalated before pH can fall.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a phosphorus awareness sampling round at a plant without chemical removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal phosphorus monitoring for information, no removal target in the current approval.

cards.label: Note any pattern linked to load or season for the supervisor review
Record flows and any industrial deliveries on the sampling days
Plot influent and effluent phosphorus together when results return
Collect influent and effluent samples at the points on the monitoring plan
File the round with the seasonal monitoring summary
Preserve and deliver the samples within the holding time on the plan

tasks.explanation: Paired influent and effluent samples with flow context give the pattern meaning, and plotting over the season is the purpose of the round.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to filamentous growth linked to low food conditions in a nutrient limited period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: microscopy shows filament types associated with low food, settling is deteriorating.

cards.label: Reduce wasting slightly to raise inventory if the supervisor approves
Review food to microorganism and solids retention time records for a low food pattern
Confirm the filament finding with a second microscopy examination
Record whether settling recovers and close the response in the process log
Check dissolved oxygen records to rule out low oxygen as the driver
Monitor settling tests and microscopy twice weekly during the response

tasks.explanation: A second examination confirms the finding before records are interpreted, oxygen is ruled out before food is blamed, and monitoring proves the response.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a basin for a temporary denitrification trial during high nitrate discharge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two week trial, one train only, the second train stays in normal operation as a control.

cards.label: Compare trial and control trains at the end of each week
Summarize the trial for the supervisor with a recommendation to adopt or stop
Collect daily nitrate and ammonia samples from both trains during the trial
Brief all shifts on the trial settings and the samples to collect
Set the trial train anoxic zone and recycle settings from the trial plan
Record baseline nitrate, ammonia, and effluent quality on both trains for several days

tasks.explanation: A baseline on both trains makes the comparison fair, the control train runs throughout, and the summary is based on paired evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking for septicity driven nutrient release in a long force main discharge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: long force main discharges to the headworks, odour and ammonia spikes noted on pump cycles.

cards.label: Resample on the new schedule to confirm the spikes have reduced
Note the times of force main pump cycles and the arrival of each slug at the headworks
Review pump run times and detention in the main for an unusually long hold
Shorten detention by adjusting pump scheduling if the supervisor approves
Log the pattern and the schedule change for future operators
Sample the arriving flow for odour, ammonia, and sulfide indication using site methods

tasks.explanation: Sampling is timed to the arriving slug so the pattern can be seen, detention is the controllable cause, and resampling proves the schedule change helped.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a weekly nutrient dashboard update for the operations team.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one page dashboard covering ammonia, nitrate, phosphorus, alkalinity, and temperature.

cards.label: Flag any result trending toward the plant action level
Add the current wasting and aeration settings beside the results
Carry any flag into the weekly operations meeting agenda
Enter the week of laboratory nutrient results in date order
Post the dashboard at the control panel for all shifts
Add wastewater temperature and average flow for the same days

tasks.explanation: Results gain meaning beside temperature, flow, and settings, flags are set from the completed picture, and the meeting receives the flags.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating rising effluent ammonia over three days.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent ammonia climbing but still below the limit in the plant approval, cold weather.

cards.label: Review wastewater temperature, solids retention time, and recent wasting changes
Check alkalinity and pH for a buffering shortfall
Make one corrective change at a time as directed by the supervisor
Check dissolved oxygen profiles for a low zone in the aeration basin
Confirm the trend with the laboratory and check for a sampling or analysis issue
Sample ammonia daily until the trend reverses and record the cause found

tasks.explanation: Analysis error is ruled out first, inventory, oxygen, and alkalinity are checked in order, and single changes let the cause be identified.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for balancing aeration between nitrification and energy use in mild weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: spring warm up, ammonia is comfortably low and aeration energy use is high.

cards.label: Review ammonia results and confirm the margin below the action level
Reduce air to the zone with the highest dissolved oxygen in one small step
Watch ammonia and dissolved oxygen daily for several days after the step
Record the seasonal air settings that held ammonia and saved energy
Repeat small steps only while ammonia stays comfortably low
Hold or reverse the step if ammonia begins to climb

tasks.explanation: Margin is proven before air is cut, steps are small and watched, and the proven settings are recorded for the next season.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting a 24 hour composite influent sample for compliance reporting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: refrigerated automatic sampler at the influent, flow paced collection.

cards.label: Retrieve the container at the end of the period and mix the composite thoroughly
Place a clean composite container and confirm refrigeration is working
Split the composite into laboratory containers, label them, and complete the custody form
Verify aliquots are being collected by checking the sampler counter mid period
Check the sampler intake line is submerged and free of debris at start up
Program the sampler for flow paced aliquots over the 24 hour period on the sampling plan

tasks.explanation: Programming and a clean cold container come before collection, a mid period check catches failure early, and thorough mixing makes the splits representative.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a duplicate and spike quality control set with a batch of effluent samples.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: laboratory quality control for a suspended solids and nutrient batch.

cards.label: Select the sample to duplicate and split it into two equal portions
Analyse the original, duplicate, and spiked portions in the same batch
Compare both values with the acceptance limits on the quality control chart
Prepare the spiked portion by adding the standard volume on the method sheet
Flag the batch and notify the supervisor if either value falls outside its limits
Calculate the duplicate agreement and the spike recovery from the results

tasks.explanation: Duplicate and spike portions must run in the same batch as the samples they judge, calculations follow analysis, and out of limit values flag the whole batch.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for calibrating a bench pH meter before a day of testing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two point calibration with standard buffers before effluent and process samples.

cards.label: Verify with an independent check standard before testing samples
Log the calibration, buffers used, and check result in the calibration record
Rinse the electrode and check it for damage or coating
Check the slope or offset reading against the acceptance range on the meter sheet
Calibrate at the first buffer and record the reading once it is stable
Rinse and calibrate at the second buffer bracketing the expected sample range

tasks.explanation: Bracketing buffers and a slope check make the calibration valid, an independent standard verifies it, and the log proves it happened.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for handling a sample that arrives at the laboratory past its holding time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent sample for bacteriological testing delivered late by a courier delay.

cards.label: Review the delivery routine to prevent a repeat and note the change
Compare the elapsed time with the holding time on the sampling plan
Collect a replacement sample at the next valid sampling opportunity
Reject the sample for compliance use and document the reason
Record the collection time, receipt time, and temperature on arrival
Notify the supervisor and the laboratory contact that the sample is compromised

tasks.explanation: Times are documented before judgement, a compromised sample is rejected rather than reported, and a replacement plus a routine fix close the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing sample bottles for a weekly sampling run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bottles needed for influent, effluent, and process samples including preserved containers.

cards.label: Select the correct container type and preservative for each analysis
Record any missing analysis in the log so it can be rescheduled
Label each bottle with location, analysis, date, and preservative before leaving the lab
Check bottle count against the plan at the vehicle before departure
Pack bottles in sampling order with the custody forms and field meters
List the analyses required from the weekly sampling plan

tasks.explanation: The plan drives container choice, labels are completed before travel, and a count check at departure prevents a wasted trip.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for reviewing a laboratory report before the results are used for compliance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly compliance report received from the contract laboratory.

cards.label: Query any missing or flagged result with the laboratory in writing
Check collection dates, receipt dates, and holding times for each result
Review quality control flags, dilutions, and detection limits noted by the lab
Check that all scheduled samples and analyses appear on the report
File the reviewed report and carry flags into the compliance summary
Compare each result with the plant approval values and flag any exceedance at once

tasks.explanation: Completeness and holding times are checked before values are trusted, exceedances are flagged immediately, and queries are documented before filing.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a chain of custody check when samples change hands.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator hands weekend samples to a courier for the contract laboratory.

cards.label: Confirm each label matches its custody line for location, date, and analysis
Have the courier sign as receiver and keep the sampler copy
Sign and date the transfer section as the relinquishing sampler
File the copy and confirm laboratory receipt the next business day
List every container on the custody form and count the physical containers
Seal the cooler and record the seal number on the form

tasks.explanation: Containers are counted against the form before sealing, signatures mark the transfer, and receipt confirmation closes the chain.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating an unusually high blank result in a solids batch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: method blank shows solids well above the usual near zero value.

cards.label: Inspect filters, dishes, and glassware used for the batch for contamination
Rerun affected samples if the new blank is clean and samples remain within holding time
Hold the batch results and do not report them until the blank is explained
Review the balance and drying oven records for the batch day
Reprepare and rerun the blank with fresh materials
Document the cause and the rerun in the quality control log

tasks.explanation: Results are held before any reporting, materials and equipment are checked in order, and reruns are justified by a clean blank.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a control chart for effluent suspended solids results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new chart to track weekly effluent solids against the plant action levels.

cards.label: Draw the centre line and the warning and action lines on the chart
Plot each new result on its sampling day from now on
Post the chart and brief operators on what a warning or action breach requires
Calculate the average and the spread used for the chart limits on the lab sheet
Gather the last several months of weekly effluent solids results
Plot the historical results in date order to confirm the chart behaves sensibly

tasks.explanation: Limits are calculated from history before lines are drawn, historical plotting tests the chart, and briefing ensures breaches trigger action.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting a grab sample for dissolved oxygen sensitive testing at the effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent sample for biochemical oxygen demand seeding checks, air exposure must be avoided.

cards.label: Label the bottle and place it in the cooler at once
Deliver to the laboratory bench within the time on the sampling plan
Record time, temperature, and weather at collection on the field sheet
Rinse the sample bottle with effluent at the sampling point
Fill the bottle by submerging it and capping it underwater or with no headspace as the method requires
Check the bottle for air bubbles and refill if any are present

tasks.explanation: Filling without air contact protects the measurement, bubbles mean a refill, and prompt cold delivery preserves the sample.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an annual laboratory method review with the contract laboratory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor and lead operator meet the contract lab to review methods, limits, and turnaround.

cards.label: Update the sampling plan and bottle list to match the agreement
Review detection limits against the approval values they must prove
Agree on method, reporting, and notification changes with the laboratory
List any new analyses required by the plant approval for the coming year
Compile the year of quality control flags, missed holding times, and late reports
File the review notes and brief all samplers on the changes

tasks.explanation: The year of problems is compiled before the meeting, new requirements are listed, and the sampling plan is updated so the agreement takes effect.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for storing and rotating laboratory reagents so expired stock is never used.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bench reagents for solids, chlorine, and nutrient testing in the plant laboratory.

cards.label: Initial and date the rotation check in the laboratory housekeeping log
Remove and set aside any expired reagent for approved disposal
Order replacements for any reagent below minimum or expiring soon
Check the stock against the minimum levels for the next month of testing
Move the earliest expiring stock to the front of each shelf
Inventory all reagents and record expiry dates on the stock sheet
